title: What a Long Strange Trip It's Been

beats.what: Marielle sets Tabitha's broken arm without anaesthesia; Tabitha is newly arrived at the settlement
The group pulls life-sized dolls from the settlement lake; Donna reads them as scarecrows keeping something in
Jade's mushroom trip begins; Boyd attempts to anchor him in the forest
Jade's trip surfaces a memory of his grandmother's death, not the answers he demanded
Jade's hallucination shows all his previous incarnations murdered by townspeople who learned the truth about him
Tabitha recovers a buried memory: the dolls were hers as a child in a previous life; when their owner died, their fears emerged from the lake

character_beats.beat: Demands the trip deliver tactical intelligence about how to go home; instead it delivers grief and then a vision that the town itself will eventually kill him
Has been passive about her memories all episode, but the doll crisis forces a breakthrough; she accesses the past-life memory that saves the group
Acts as Jade's anchor and safety net throughout the trip, but is himself showing tremors and a possible hallucination that he hides from Jade

key_lines.line: Show me what I used to know that I can't remember. Show me what's in here that'll help us leave.
key_lines.why: Jade's framing of the trip as a retrieval mission; the episode then refuses that framing

key_lines.line: None of them are ripped apart. These men were murdered.
key_lines.why: The revelation that Jade's previous deaths were by human hands, not creatures

key_lines.line: I know what we have to do to go home. I know how we can save the children.
key_lines.why: The episode's closing turn: Jade emerges from the trip with what he believes is a complete answer

open_loops: Jade says he knows how to save the children and get home; no one else has heard the specifics yet
The dolls were put back in the lake as scarecrows, but what they contain is now known; will that entity surface again?
Boyd's tremors and possible hallucination suggest personal deterioration he is not disclosing
Marielle had a breakdown in the ambulance during the episode; its cause is unnamed

payoffs.what: The Lake of Tears phrase reaches its first concrete payoff: the settlement lake is not the Lake of Tears, but the memory Tabitha recovers from it is a past-life fragment about dolls thrown into a lake, linking the lake motif from the earliest episodes to Tabitha's reincarnation arc

contradiction.wants: A controlled retrieval of tactical knowledge about how to break the trap
contradiction.does: Opens himself to uncontrolled visions that include his own repeated murder at the hands of the people he is trying to save

tone_notes: The episode sustains a 65.6 words/min average, the second lowest in the season, but the density map is violently spiky rather than evenly quiet. Two silences over 50 seconds anchor the trip sequence: 09:19-10:13 (55 sec) before the dolls surface, and 34:20-35:12 (52 sec) inside Jade's vision of his murdered past selves. The density spike at minute 33 (161 words/min) is the highest single-minute count of the episode and lands exactly on the moment Jade realizes the nature of his deaths.
